$comment: CAN1_TERM: shrink the +5V plane cut from 9.699 mm to 1.508 mm.
This is NOT the same fix CAN2's stub got. That one moved wholesale to the
bottom layer because both endpoints were through-hole and the corridor was
empty. Here R10.1 and H1.2 are separated by two full-width barriers at almost
the same latitude -- +3V3 on the top at y=128.095 and CAN1_RX on the bottom at
y=128.023 -- so neither outer layer can carry the crossing, which is exactly
why the import used an inner layer. Going around costs either a 20 mm detour
east of U8 or a squeeze through a 0.51 mm gap between CAN1_RX's via and the
GND bus at (155.7,122.3). Neither is worth it on a fab-bound board.
What IS worth it: only the crossing itself needs to be on the plane. The stub
now runs bottom-layer from H1.2 down to a new via at (166.872,127.350), hops
1.508 mm north-to-south on Inner2 past both barriers, and rejoins the existing
via at (166.872,128.858). Cost is one extra via on a DC termination jumper leg.
Via clearances, all against the 0.534 mm a 0.6 via needs from a 0.254 track:
new via to +3V3 0.745, to CAN1_RX 0.673, to CAN1_L's corridor far. The bottom
swath x164-174 / y121.5-127.5 was verified empty on all four layers.
